game: Romancing SaGa 2: Revenge of the Seven
data_notes: Item names and source descriptions are preserved in English.
Missing values are omitted rather than inferred.
Original source terminology and strategic notes are retained in English.
A potency value of null means the source did not state one.

general_notes.title: Sword techniques
general_notes.text: Unless otherwise mentioned, sword techs deal damage based on STR. Accuracy depends on STR and SPD.

categories.name: Swords (1h Swords)
categories.description: Unless otherwise mentioned, sword techs deal damage based on STR. Accuracy depends on STR and SPD.

techniques.name: Parry
effects: An alternative to Defend. User will deflect physical attacks.
sparked_from: Using any Sword attack while attacked by an enemy
techniques.notes: Unlike in other SaGa games it will not auto-trigger just by being in a tech list and must be used to activate during the round.

techniques.name: Stun Slash
techniques.notes: When used as part of a Unity attack, due to English localization mistakes it has the prefix of ‘Knee’ or affix of ‘Split’.

techniques.name: Mince
techniques.notes: The battle tooltip says “Has large damage variance”. This appears to be nonsense. The attack hits six times consistently and the damage dealt per hit is the normal expected range.

categories.name: Greatsword (2h Swords)
categories.description: The Original Japanese names for these techniques reference Japanese swordsmanship, which is completely lost in the English localization.

techniques.name: Deflect
effects: An alternative to Defend. User will deflect physical attacks.
sparked_from: Using any 2h sword attack while attacked by an enemy
techniques.notes: Unlike in other SaGa games it will not auto-trigger just by being in a tech list and must be used to activate during the round.

techniques.name: Hard Slash
effects: Physical Melee damage to one enemy
techniques.notes: The English localization of the Remaster named this ‘Blunt Strike’, which is confusing because that is what the Remake calls the second Greatsword tech. Mine-uchi is a Kendo technique and does not mean “Hard Slash”; it means “strike to the head”. In the original and Remaster, this attack inflicted the Stun ailment.

techniques.name: Blunt Strike
effects: A melee attack that attempts to Stun
techniques.notes: Prior SaGa games localized this as Sunder. Maki-uchi is a Kendo technique that strikes the head; it does not mean Sunder. It means “Rolling Strike”, referring to the way the blade rolls off the left arm before attacking.
